description: Where a landing's time goes, one point per land.sh run. land.sh writes a logfmt line to syslog from its EXIT trap (`logger -t landing-annotation`), promtail ships it to Loki, and this board reads it. wait_merge is `--await-merge` polling until the PR merged; wait_ci is master CI on the merge commit, plus any wait on a newer tip when another PR merged mid-landing; deploy is the wait on the promotion that applies the merge, because no landing runs deploy.sh since #7349. Earlier rows booked the scoped deploy.sh run under deploy. Empty phases were never reached (a `blocked` landing has no wait_ci). `cause` names which stop a `deploy-failed` verdict was. One exit-75 verdict carries one too: `deferred`, with `promote-timeout`, `gate-unreadable` or `gate-stale`. Rows before #7349 also show the retired `tip-outran-retries` with `deploy-exit-4`. Every other verdict leaves it empty, and the cause panel counts every landing whose cause is not empty. Rows written before H7.49a, which stopped land.sh running the GitOps tick, also carry the retired `tick`, `lock`, `holder` and `kick` fields; Loki's 744h retention drops the last of them around 2026-12-07, and no panel reads them. Every panel drops the test fixtures the `land.sh` suite wrote to the real syslog until 2026-09-03 (`_no_syslog` in scripts/deploy_tools/tests/conftest.py closed the leak). They are 8,282 of the 8,777 records Loki holds, and the discriminator is the PR id alone: `pr` 939, 999 and 999999 are the numbers the fixtures pass, and `pr=unknown` was an argparse failure that reached the EXIT trap before the ledger had a PR, so those rows carry no sha and no phase timing. Issue #1304 stopped the emitter writing `unknown` rows at all, so the ones in Loki are historic and the filter keeps dropping them for the rest of the 744h retention window. The regex is anchored because `pr !~ "999"` unanchored also eats `pr=999999` and would eat a real PR 1999 later. Do NOT add `sha!=""`: a real landing that aborts before the merge has an empty sha too, and filtering on it removes most genuine `aborted` rows. CLI equivalent: `uv run python scripts/diagnostics/probe.py loki-query '{job="syslog"} |= "event=landing" | logfmt | pr !~ "^(939|999|999999|unknown)$"'`.

panels.description: Seconds spent in each phase, one colour per phase. A point is the longest landing in its interval, so on a wide range two landings close together show as one. `keep` drops the labels logfmt extracts, which otherwise make each landing its own series. A tall wait_merge is PR CI or a PR nobody armed; a tall wait_ci is the master sweep; a tall deploy is rollout and stabilisation waits.

targets.expr: max_over_time({job="syslog"} |= "event=landing" | logfmt | pr !~ "^(939|999|999999|unknown)$" | keep wait_merge | unwrap wait_merge [$__interval])
max_over_time({job="syslog"} |= "event=landing" | logfmt | pr !~ "^(939|999|999999|unknown)$" | keep wait_ci | unwrap wait_ci [$__interval])
max_over_time({job="syslog"} |= "event=landing" | logfmt | pr !~ "^(939|999|999999|unknown)$" | keep deploy | unwrap deploy [$__interval])
max_over_time({job="syslog"} |= "event=landing" | logfmt | pr !~ "^(939|999|999999|unknown)$" | keep total | unwrap total [$__interval])

panels.description: Median over the selected range. This is the number to compare week to week before touching CI sharding or the deploy's soak windows.

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.5, {job="syslog"} |= "event=landing" | logfmt | pr !~ "^(939|999|999999|unknown)$" | keep wait_merge | unwrap wait_merge [$__range])
quantile_over_time(0.5, {job="syslog"} |= "event=landing" | logfmt | pr !~ "^(939|999|999999|unknown)$" | keep wait_ci | unwrap wait_ci [$__range])
quantile_over_time(0.5, {job="syslog"} |= "event=landing" | logfmt | pr !~ "^(939|999|999999|unknown)$" | keep deploy | unwrap deploy [$__range])
quantile_over_time(0.5, {job="syslog"} |= "event=landing" | logfmt | pr !~ "^(939|999|999999|unknown)$" | keep total | unwrap total [$__range])

panels.title: Medians over the range

panels.description: How the landings in the range ended. settled and nothing-to-deploy are the two that delivered; everything else stopped early. `aborted` is the EXIT-trap default, so it means a path that named no verdict rather than one particular failure. Measured 2026-09-06 over the default 7d range: 43 aborted of 495 real landings (8.7%), against 6,326 of 8,777 (72%) before the fixture filter.
panels.title: Landings by verdict

panels.description: Every landing that recorded a cause, counted by that cause. Most are a deploy-failed verdict, and the verdict alone does not say what went live. tag-miss names a tag nothing applies, while promote and Flux still apply the rest of master. promote-held is DEPLOY_HOLD holding the promotion. soak-failed means Flux applied the revision and its soak then failed, so the change is live. One exit-75 verdict carries a cause too: deferred, with promote-timeout, with gate-unreadable or gate-stale when the health gate graded nothing. Rows before #7349 also show the retired host-lookup, playbook-failed and deploy-exit-* causes, and rows before H7.49a the retired tick-held and tick-failed. Landings by verdict tells those apart from a deploy-failed. Every other verdict leaves cause empty, so it is not counted here.
panels.title: Landings by cause

panels.description: The raw lines, newest first: pr, sha, verdict, the cause behind a deploy-failed, exit code, every phase, and the tags deployed. A verdict other than settled or nothing-to-deploy is a landing that stopped early; its phases show where.
